title: New Demand Economics: Education, Demand Upgrading, and Structural Change
abstract: arXiv:2510.17121v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Education can change what households buy as well as what workers produce. We study this demand channel in a two-sector growth model. Education shifts spending toward an education-sensitive bundle, drawing labor into the sector that supplies it. Learning lowers its relative price. When substitution between the bundles is strong enough, the price decline raises its expenditure share and reinforces the initial shift. The balance between this feedback and technological catch-up determines the long-run allocation. Weak feedback gives a unique stable configuration. Strong feedback can sustain two stable configurations with different expenditure shares, so the long-run outcome depends on initial productivity. A sufficiently large, attainable increase in education removes the low-share configuration. This transition can occur through demand alone, without a direct productivity effect of education. translated_title: 新需求经济学：教育、需求升级与结构变迁
translated_abstract: 教育既能改变家庭购买什么，也能改变工人生产什么。我们在一个两部门增长模型中研究这一需求渠道。教育使支出转向对教育敏感的商品组合，从而吸引劳动力进入供应该组合的部门。学习降低了该组合的相对价格。当两个组合之间的替代性足够强时，价格下降会提高其支出份额并强化最初的转移。这种反馈与技术追赶之间的平衡决定了长期的资源配置。弱反馈会产生唯一稳定的配置；强反馈则可以维持两个具有不同支出份额的稳定配置，因此长期结果取决于初始生产率。足够大的、可实现的受教育程度提升可以消除低份额配置。这种结构转变可以仅通过需求实现，而无需教育产生直接的生产率效应。早期的消费承诺也可以改变……（摘要被截断）
tldr: 该论文在两部门增长模型中揭示了教育驱动结构变迁的需求渠道：教育改变消费结构并吸引劳动力，当替代性足够强时形成反馈循环与多重均衡，足够大的教育提升可仅凭需求力量——而非生产率效应——消除低支出份额均衡，实现经济结构升级。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a demand channel through which education drives structural change in a two-sector growth model: education shifts consumption patterns and labor allocation, and when substitution is strong enough, multiple equilibria emerge—allowing a sufficiently large, attainable rise in education to trigger structural upgrading through demand alone, without any direct productivity effect.
